subject: Chemistry
title: Debye-Hückel-Onsager Model & Kohlrausch’s Law Applications
topics: Variation of κ (decreases with dilution) and Λ_m (increases with dilution)
Debye-Hückel-Onsager Linear Equation for Strong Electrolytes (Λ_m = Λ°_m - A√C)
Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions (Λ°_m(A_x B_y) = x λ°_+ + y λ°_-)
Applications: Limiting Molar Conductivity of Weak Electrolytes, Degree of Dissociation (α = Λ_m / Λ°_m), and Sparingly Soluble Salt Solubility (S = 1000 κ / Λ°_m)
quickSummary: Conductivity κ decreases on dilution (fewer ions per cm³). Molar conductivity Λ_m increases on dilution. Strong electrolytes obey Λ_m = Λ°_m - A√C. Kohlrausch's law: Λ°_m = Σ ν_i λ°_i. Used to find α = Λ_m/Λ°_m and K_sp = S² where S = (1000·κ)/Λ°_m.
summary: Master dilution effects on conductance, Debye-Hückel-Onsager extrapolation, and Kohlrausch's Law calculations.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Dilution Trends & Debye-Hückel-Onsager Model
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Dilution Trends & Debye-Hückel-Onsager Model

summaryBox.title: Dilution Trends
summaryBox.takeaway: Conductivity κ DECREASES with dilution (fewer ions per cm³). Molar conductivity Λ_m INCREASES with dilution. Weak electrolytes cannot be extrapolated to √C = 0.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DEBYE-HÜCKEL-ONSAGER EQUATION (STRONG ELECTROLYTES)

Λ_m = Λ°_m - A √C

• Strong electrolytes (KCl, NaCl): Linear decrease with √C; intercept at C=0 gives Λ°_m.
• Weak electrolytes (CH₃COOH): Non-linear steep curve near C=0; CANNOT be extrapolated!
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Conductivity ($\kappa$)**: **Decreases with dilution** because the number of current-carrying ions per unit volume ($1\text{ cm}^3$) decreases.
• **Molar Conductivity ($\Lambda_m$)**: **Increases with dilution** because inter-ionic attractions decrease (for strong electrolytes) or dissociation degree $\alpha \to 1.0$ (for weak electrolytes).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Kohlrausch's Law & Quantitative Applications
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Kohlrausch's Law & Quantitative Applications
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
KOHLRAUSCH'S LAW APPLICATIONS

1. Weak Electrolyte Λ°_m:
   Λ°_m(CH₃COOH) = Λ°_m(CH₃COONa) + Λ°_m(HCl) - Λ°_m(NaCl)

2. Degree of Dissociation & K_a:
   α = Λ_m / Λ°_m  ⟹  K_a = (C α²) / (1 - α)

3. Solubility of Sparingly Soluble Salts:
   S (mol/L) = (1000 × κ) / Λ°_m  ⟹  K_sp = S² (for AB salts like AgCl)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Kohlrausch’s Law**: At infinite dilution, each ion contributes independently to limiting molar conductivity:
$$\mathbf{\Lambda_m^\circ (A_x B_y) = x \cdot \lambda_m^\circ (A^{y+}) + y \cdot \lambda_m^\circ (B^{x-})}$$
• **Degree of Ionization**: $\mathbf{\alpha = \frac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ}}$ and $K_a = \frac{C \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$.
• **Solubility of Sparingly Soluble Salts**: $\mathbf{S = \frac{1000 \cdot \kappa}{\Lambda_m^\circ}}$ (in $\text{mol/L}$).

quickRevision: κ decreases with dilution; Λ_m increases with dilution.
Kohlrausch's law: Λ°_m = x λ°_+ + y λ°_-.
α = Λ_m / Λ°_m and S = (1000·κ) / Λ°_m.
